:::{#rem-kappa-prevalence}
#### Kappa depends on prevalence

When both classifiers call one [class](#def-class) rarely,
the [chance agreement](#def-chance-agreement) $p_e$ is close to 1,
so the same [overall agreement](#def-overall-agreement) leaves little room for agreement beyond chance,
and [Cohen's kappa](#def-cohen-kappa) can be low even when the overall agreement is high,
as @exm-kappa-paradox shows.
@cicchetti1990high recommend reporting
the [positive agreement](#def-positive-agreement) and [negative agreement](#def-negative-agreement) alongside Cohen's kappa,
so that poor agreement on the rarer class is not hidden.

Source: @feinstein1990high; @cicchetti1990high.

:::
